short: The single day in 1066 that replaced England's ruling class.
full:
On 14 October 1066, William, Duke of Normandy, met Harold Godwinson's army on Senlac Hill near Hastings. Harold had marched south at extraordinary speed, having defeated a Norwegian invasion at Stamford Bridge nineteen days earlier.

The English shield wall held for most of a long day. It broke when Norman feigned retreats — or genuine ones exploited opportunistically — drew defenders off the ridge. Harold was killed, and with him both his brothers. William was crowned on Christmas Day. Within twenty years almost the entire Anglo-Saxon aristocracy had been dispossessed, the language of government became French, and England was reoriented from Scandinavia towards continental Europe.
